messages:
maya: Heads-up — AcmePayments (ticket #AP-8129) hit a failure in structured_output mode. They get a 400 parse error when the input contains CRLF and backslashes. Customer says it worked last week. Logs attached below.

samira: Thanks, Maya. I have the customer's minimal payload: they send a customer note with Windows line endings and quotes. Repro steps and payload below.

samira: ```json
{
  \"customer_id\": \"acme-42\",
  \"note\": \"Line1\r\\nLine2 \"quoted\" \\ backslash and emoji: \uD83D\uDE00\"
}
```

samira: cURL they used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{\"model\":\"open-struct-v2\",\"structured_output\":true,\"input\":{\"customer_id\":\"acme-42\",\"note\":\"Line1\\r\\nLine2 \"quoted\" \\ backslash\"}}'
```

maya: API response body (400):
```
{
  \"error\": \"parse_error\",
  \"message\": \"Invalid JSON in model output: unexpected token at position 37\"
}
```

alex: I looked at the support logs and I see the model's raw output contains literal CRLF sequences plus some already-escaped backslashes. It looks like our JSON serializer may be double-escaping backslashes when normalizing newlines from the tokenizer. Snippet from runtime log (model output quoted):

eng-ml-bot: ```
GENERATED_RAW: Line1\r\nLine2 \"quoted\" \\ backslash
SERIALIZER_OUT: {\"summary\": \"Line1\\r\\nLine2 \"quoted\" \\\\ backslash\"}
```

alex: Notice SERIALIZER_OUT has \\\\ backslash (4 slashes) which becomes a literal \\ in the final response and breaks downstream JSON parsing for customers using strict parsers.

jordan: Can repro locally with model=open-struct-v2@v2.1-quant, structured_output=true, and input containing CRLF. Minimal repro provided.

jordan: ```bash
# minimal repro
echo '{\"input\":\"Line1\r\nLine2 \"x\" \\ test\"}' > payload.json
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @payload.json
```

jordan: Running this shows parse_error on the response when piping through jq. Seems serializer is applying JSON.stringify twice on some branches of the streaming path.

maya: Customer workaround: pre-replace CRLF with \n and escape backslashes on their side before sending. They confirmed that works but want us to fix it — they can't rely on altering client behavior.

samira: I escalated to eng-runtime and attached the ticket with the raw binary log + base64 of the model output. Ticket: ENGESC-2026.

jordan: I opened a quick patch to stop double-serializing in the stream buffer (PR #987). The PR changes the stream chunk handler to check an `isEscaped` flag instead of unconditionally running JSON.stringify. Running canary in 10% now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary=10% from branch fix/avoid-double-serialize (#987) — pipeline passed.

alex: Also note: content-type header from the model path was `application/json; charset=utf-8` so most clients assume valid JSON. Our system shouldn't emit malformed JSON just because the model emitted CRLF or unicode escapes.

jordan: I'll follow up if canary looks good; initial tests show structured responses with CRLF now preserved as `\\r\\n` (escaped) consistently instead of introducing extra slashes.

samira: Customer updated: they can wait for a fix but requested ETA. Maya — any ETA we can give?

maya: Tentative ETA: if canary is clean, roll to stable in ~4h. I'll update ticket AP-8129 and ping once it's live.

samira: Customer appreciated the workaround and will hold for the patch. Marking P2 for now; will upgrade to P1 if they hit production outage.

jordan: Postmortem note: root cause appears to be newline normalization + conditional escaping applied both at tokenizer normalization and at stream chunk finalizer. Added unit tests for CRLF + backslash combos.

maya: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread open until stable rollout and customer confirmation. :thumbsup:
